thread:
maria-l: Heads up — seeing a persistent nvme latency bubble in eu-west3 starting ~03:00 UTC. GPU pods getting preempted as disk reads spike to 180-400ms for small random reads. Anyone oncall?

raj: Confirmed. Evictions between 03:12-03:18 UTC on gnode-34x and gnode-35y. IOPS stayed normal but avg latency exploded. Kernel log snippet: 
```
[  810.123456] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[  810.123457] blk_update_request: error -5 on sector 123456
```

samir: This time window coincides with the ephemeral-scrub cron. We had scrub concurrency bumped to 32 last week for faster cleanup — might be thrashing the scheduler + heavy seek pattern.

maria-l: scrub job is scheduled 03:00 by janitor in that AZ. Did the job overlap with batch GPU provisioning?

raj: Yes, batch provisioning spiked too; GPU scheduling created lots of short-lived snapshots and small IOs. Combined load looks bad.

janet: Ops suggestion: emergency mitigation = reduce janitor scrub concurrency to 6 for eu-west3 and add a soft rate_limit (50MB/s). Also move scrub start to 01:00 for a 4h window away from batch jobs.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2029 nvme-latency-eu-west3 — pager duty notified :rotating_light: 

samir: I like the concurrency/rate limits. Also can we enable per-node blkio cgroup limits for janitor and set io.sched to deadline on the affected nodes? That should bound worst-case tail latency.

maria-l: Agreed. Quick rollout plan: 1) patch janitor config for eu-west3 (concurrency=6, rate_limit=50MB/s) 2) change scrub cron to 01:00 3) set io.sched=deadline + blkio limits on gnode-* in the AZ 4) monitor 2h.

raj: If software mitigations fail, we should budget drive replacements — estimate ~$12k per rack for NVMe refresh (procurement lead time 3-4w). But let's avoid that unless SMART/failure counts increase.

janet: I'll push the janitor config change to canary nodes first (gnode-34x), then roll. I'll also add a temporary k8s taint to avoid new GPU allocations on the hottest hosts until we confirm stability.

maria-l: Thanks. Please paste the monitoring dashboard and perf baselines here after canary. If tail p95 stays <30ms we can revert the taint.

ops-bot: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nvme-tail-latency (added to incident).

raj: quick note — capture fio profiles of random reads (4k, ioengine=libaio, iodepth=32) before/after change for a baseline.

maria-l: on it. will collect samples and post results in the incident thread. :thumbsup:
